inputs.diff_summary: Java accepts stereotype-before-color explicit cloud syntax and renders a cloud cluster; Rust misses the cloud declaration and renders only top-level classes.
Java emits italic stereotype text above the bold cloud title; Rust emits only the bold title at the stereotype y-position, shifting subsequent element order.

findings.summary: Explicit cloud clusters with stereotypes are not modeled like Java.
findings.evidence: checker_cluster_tb_explicit_cloud_stereo_no_color_complex.puml fails. Java USymbolCloud.asBig draws stereotype at y=13 and title at 13 + stereotype height; Rust emit_layout_cloud_cluster measures and emits only the bold title at CLOUD_TITLE_BASELINE.
findings.scope: cluster title/intrinsic dimension ownership gap on a valid explicit-cloud perturbation; this is account-adjacent because the account claims final cloud dimensions are owned by the translated cluster model but does not cover the title/stereotype stack that feeds those dimensions.

findings.summary: Rust package parsing rejects Java-valid stereotype-before-color explicit cloud declarations.
findings.evidence: checker_cluster_tb_explicit_cloud_stereo_complex.puml is accepted by Java CommandPackageWithUSymbol, where stereotype/tags/url appear before color, but Rust try_package requires optional #color before optional <<stereotype>>. Rust then renders only top-level classes.
findings.scope: valid PlantUML parser divergence on explicit cloud plus stereotype/color; not a post-normalization arithmetic falsification by itself.

findings.summary: The post-normalization endpoint-width account survived the plain controls.
findings.evidence: Plain explicit TB cloud, explicit LR nested cloud, packageStyle LR nested cloud, and packageStyle TB compact cloud all matched Java structurally through diff_one --no-oracle.
findings.scope: supports the account for unstereotyped cloud cluster dimensions across TB/LR, explicit/packageStyle, nested/linked, and compact/wider label cases.

verdict_reason: The endpoint-reconstruction account is supported by the plain controls, but valid held-out explicit-cloud stereotype cases fail. Because the requested validation includes explicit cloud and topology axes, and the failing cases exercise Java-accepted syntax and cluster title geometry, this mechanism cannot be accepted under the T14 held-out adversarial gate.
